title: CUDA/NCCL K8s probe lab notes (variance log)
content:
Summary:
This is a lab-oriented variance log capturing a set of empirical probes and short-run validations around upgrading Kubernetes worker images + NVIDIA driver + CUDA + NCCL across heterogeneous on-prem racks. Objective: come up with a compact validation runbook (fast checks) and a set of hard-fail signatures to gate automated TF module rollouts.

Why this file exists (purpose):
- Capture unexpected cross-version behaviors observed in the last two weeks of test runs (edge case reproductions).
- Produce a minimal validation matrix for CI that can catch the top-5 regressions we actually hit.
- Collect Terraform module notes (variables/ordering) that matter when swapping node image/userdata for driver upgrades.

Test environment (high level):
- Kubernetes: 1.26.7, 1.27.4 (separate clusters)
- Kubelet/container runtime: containerd 1.7.2 with runc; crictl for probes
- GPUs: mixture of A10G (driver 535.x) and A30 (driver 525.x) nodes in same cluster (heterogeneous pool)
- OS images: ubuntu-22.04 (custom node image), centos-8-stream (lab)
- CUDA versions tested: 11.8, 12.0, 12.1
- NCCL versions tested: 2.14.x, 2.15.x, 2.17.x
- NVIDIA driver installer modes: runfile + dkms (where available) and package from vendor (deb/rpm)
- TF modules: terraform-aws-eks-style module adapted for on-prem (node pool lifecycle via image_id userdata)

Minimal validation matrix (condensed):
(Interpretation: P = pass on short microbench, F = fail/hang, W = intermittent/variance)

Node image | Driver | CUDA | NCCL | microbench(all-reduce 8x1GB) | observed failure mode
ubuntu-22.04-A10G | 535.54 | 12.0 | 2.17.4 | P | --
ubuntu-22.04-A30  | 525.85 | 11.8 | 2.14.3 | W | occasional hang at step 3 (10-30s stall)
centos8-A10G      | 535.54 | 12.1 | 2.15.6 | P | increased p2p latency (~15%)
ubuntu-22.04-A30  | 525.85 | 12.0 | 2.17.4 | F | NCCL init timeout (stacktrace shows transport negotiation failure)
ubuntu-22.04-A30  | 535.54 | 12.1 | 2.17.4 | P | --

Key observations and hypotheses (unique/empirical):
1) Heterogeneous-driver pools produce the most subtle failures. If 2 nodes in an all-reduce run use different driver families (525 vs 535) there is an elevated probability of NCCL transport selection mismatch. Hypothesis: driver ABI divergence changes top-of-stack transport ordering, which surfaces as long-tail stalls.
2) NCCL 2.17.x is more resilient across mixed CUDA minor versions, but only when drivers are >= 535. On A30 with older drivers (525 series) we saw init negotiation failures when peer selected net/dev path requiring latest patches.
3) dkms vs package-managed drivers: dkms-installed drivers on nodes rebuilt kernel modules on image boot and occasionally produced a new minor-version module (e.g., 525.90 -> 525.92) after recompile; this mismatch between module version and userland library produced silent degrade rather than explicit errors.
4) Some centos kernels with retpoline backports showed ~10-20% overhead on p2p benchmarks; rarely a functional failure but relevant for SLOs.
5) Kubernetes CNI MTU fragmentation can amplify NCCL stalls for large messages; our microbench with 1GB shards hit edge cases on MTU=1400 causing retransmit/backpressure loops.

Failure signatures to block rollouts (clear, automatable):
- NCCL init timeout: container logs contain "NCCL WARN INIT" and processes stuck beyond 45s during init phase.
- Persistent all-reduce stalls: all-reduce round does not complete within 3x median baseline (baselined from known-good runs).
- GPU health mismatch: nvidia-smi shows compute processes but kernel driver mismatch shown in dmesg (messages about "nvidia: module verification failed" or "kernel module version mismatch with userland").
- DKMS rebuild drift: checksum of /usr/lib64/libnvidia-*.so vs installed package list differs after boot.

Quick validation (local probe commands to include in CI node test):
- Driver / CUDA basic:
  sudo nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version,name,memory.total --format=csv
  python - <<'PY'
import torch; print(torch.cuda.is_available()); print(torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0))
PY
- NCCL microbench: use NCCL-tests container (nccl-tests: v2.17)
  docker run --gpus all --rm nccl/nccl-tests:2.17.0 bash -lc '\n    /usr/local/nccl-tests/build/all_reduce_perf -b 8 -e 1024M -f 2 -g 4'
  watch for completion < 120s for 8x1GB across 4 GPUs on same host; across hosts expect < 3x baseline.
- P2P sanity:
  python -c "import socket; s=socket.socket(); s.bind(('0.0.0.0',0)); print('ok')" (simple)
  nvidia-smi topo --matrix
- Kernel/userland consistency check (fast):
  sudo grep -i "NVRM" /var/log/kern.log || sudo dmesg | tail -n 200 | grep -i nvidia
  sha256sum /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libnvidia-*.so | sed -n '1,20p'

Terraform notes (ordering and gotchas observed):
- Upgrade pattern we used (works more reliably in lab):
  1) Create a new node image (AMI/iso) with desired driver + cuda preinstalled; bake & test images in staging.
  2) Add new nodepool with image_id pointing to new image (keep old pool live).
  3) Drain and cordon a small percentage (5-10%) of old nodes and move replica workloads to new pool.
  4) Run NCCL microbench across mixed pools; observe for 24h.
  5) If green, progressively scale down old pool.
- DO NOT run in-place driver upgrades via userdata on a node that is running GPU workloads. We saw ~30% failure rate where kubelet restarted before driver DKMS rebuilt kernel module, leaving containers with mismatched symbols.
- Terraform ordering: ensure nodepool terraform resource uses "create_before_destroy = true" or equivalent lifecycle to avoid all-at-once replacement.
- When using cloud-init userdata to install drivers, include an explicit reboot step and a post-reboot validation script that exits non-zero if validation fails. We use systemd oneshot unit that blocks Kube join until driver check passes.

Observed intermittent behaviors (notes to capture for future debugging):
- Some driver packages drop udev rules that change device file group ownership causing container runtimes to lose access (permission denied inside container).
- Net plugin reconfigure timing: when CNI restarts during node upgrade, NCCL transports that rely on ibverbs can flake if device registration reorders.
- Kubelet ephemeral configuration: we observed node annotations lost during quick reboots (race in our cluster-autoscaler hooks).

Runbook: upgrade-fast-checklist (short):
- Before upgrade: capture baseline metrics (nvidia-smi topo, p2p latency, nccl baseline run), dump running GPU processes list.
- Step 0: Bake image w/ drivers and CUDA tested on identical kernel.
- Step 1: Add small new pool; ensure taints/labels consistent for scheduling rules.
- Step 2: Run smoke nccl test between new pool nodes and a known-good node from old pool. Abort on any of the failure signatures.
- Step 3: Roll 10% of production traffic (canary) on new pool; monitor traces for increased tail latency on generation/embedding endpoints.
- Step 4: If sustained errors, repro locally by bringing up ephemeral 2-node cluster with the same driver mismatch pattern.

Hardening recommendations (practical):
- Add a checksum/driver-version assertion in the node agent startup. Fail node join if driver/userland mismatch present.
- Add NCCL-test job to CI/CD that runs at least once per week against staging mixed-pool cluster with random pairings.
- Prefer homogenized driver families within any given all-reduce job scheduling domain (scheduler label enforcement).
- Include MTU-probing in network validation (automate iperf and large message send/recv tests).

Open questions / next experiments:
- Does backporting a small patch to 525 driver series (security patch release) remove the NCCL init timeout? Need to test 525.92+ on A30 specifically.
- Could container-level LD_PRELOAD of userland library shim mask subtle ABI drift? (dangerous, but worth controlled lab test).
- Better kernel compatibility matrix: expand tests across Ubuntu 24.04 kernels and RHEL-derived 8/9 variants.

Attachments / quick references (what to copy into tickets):
- log snippets for NCCL init timeout (search term: "NCCL WARN INIT")
- dkms-rebuild fingerprint mismatch steps (commands and files to collect)
- short terraform lifecycle snippet we used in test repo: 
  resource "onprem_node_pool" "gpu_new" {
    image_id = var.new_image_id
    lifecycle { create_before_destroy = true }
  }

Notes to self (informal):
- Ethan: follow up on 525->535 lab patch on A30 hardware next week.
- Lucia: add nccl-tests runner to nightly cluster tests; configure to run across random node pairings.
- Samir: add a CI job that runs the kernel/userland consistency checks after image bake.

If we want a shorter "policy" for automatic rollouts: fail-fast on any of the enumerated failure signatures; allow automatic canary if microbench passes and driver checksums match.

End of doc.
